whatThisVerifierFoundAboutThatClaim: The residual defect count is confirmed exactly. Running the completeness verifier here across the nine families totals 46: knownRequiredFieldsMissing 32, incompleteRows 4, requiredOptionsMissing 10, and zero on the other six counters. FIX-A reported 46.
ri_nonconviction_sealing-set is confirmed at zero on all nine counters.

The byte-identical claim is confirmed for every unchanged-official component. Those components are deliberately not committed, because committing a source body is forbidden, and each one's recorded hash AND byte length bind exactly to that official form's entry in the committed corpus index. An unchanged copy is what the record says and what the hashes show.

All 13 source documents across the nine families bind exactly to the committed corpus index, with zero near-collisions. Captain asked whether the corrupted-pin pattern found in SRC01 touches these families: it does not.
whyEveryFamilyStillFails: The 46 residual defects are real and FIX-A said so; they are not overclaiming. But a residual defect is still a defect, so every family is FAIL_REPAIR_REQUIRED rather than a pass. Four families additionally fail a filing-guidance obligation the nine counters do not measure at all, which is why ri_nonconviction_sealing-set fails on FEE_AND_WAIVER while its nine counters read zero.

That was this harness's error, not a packet defect: the absent files are all unchanged-official components whose bytes must not be committed. The check now binds their recorded hashes to the committed corpus index and they pass. No repair assignment was raised on that basis.
